item.title: Researchers propose quantum Earth observation for photon-limited environments
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: Have you ever wondered what Earth observation satellites see when they look down at the deep ocean or a dense tropical forest during the dead of night? The answer, for the most part, is nothing. Standard optical sensors require a steady stream of light to function, and in these photon-limited regions, they hit a hard physical boundary.
Waypoint’s Take: For someone heading outside, the useful question is observational: watch for phenology cues — bloom, leaf-out, senescence — that mark the season. item.description:
